title: Lens & mirror formula
examples: What is the difference between the lens formula and the mirror formula?
How do I know which sign to use for the object distance?
Can you explain what magnification means for a real image?

explain.say: Today we are learning the lens and mirror formulas. These help us find distances and sizes.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a convex lens. Look at the convex lens, the object and the focal point. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The first formula relates focal length, image distance, and object distance. Remember the sign rules for these values.
For concave mirrors and lenses, the focal length is negative. This is an important rule to remember always.
Magnification tells us how much bigger or smaller the image is. It is calculated by the ratio v over u.
Let us look at a concave mirror example. If the object is placed at twice the focal length, the image forms at the same point.
In real life, consider a dentist using a mirror. They use the mirror formula to position the image correctly for examination.

faq.q: Do I use the same formula for lenses and mirrors?
faq.a: Yes, the mathematical formulas are the same for both lenses and mirrors. However, the sign conventions for focal length might differ slightly depending on the specific textbook you use.
asks: Is the math the same for both types of optics?

faq.q: When is the image formed virtually?
faq.a: An image is virtual when the reflected or refracted rays appear to come from a point, but they do not actually pass through it. For virtual images, the image distance v will be negative.
asks: How do I tell if an image is virtual?
What does a negative v mean?

faq.q: What does the sign of magnification tell me?
faq.a: The sign tells you about the orientation. A negative magnification means the image is inverted. A positive magnification means the image is upright.
asks: Does the sign of m mean it's flipped?

faq.q: If I get a negative result for v, is that always the answer?
faq.a: Not always. You must check the physical setup and the sign conventions for that specific mirror or lens. A negative v usually indicates a virtual image.
asks: What does a negative image distance imply?

faq.q: Is the focal length always positive for converging optics?
faq.a: No. For concave mirrors and diverging lenses, the focal length is considered negative according to standard sign conventions. This helps keep the math consistent.
asks: Do concave objects have negative focal lengths?

facts: For concave mirrors, the focal length (f) is negative.
Magnification (m) is calculated as negative v divided by u.
A negative value for v indicates a virtual image.

quiz.say: A convex lens forms a real image at a distance of 15 centimeters. If the object is placed at 10 centimeters, what is the focal length?
quiz.why: The formula for a convex lens is 1/f = 1/v - 1/u. Plugging in v=15 and u=10 gives 1/f = 1/15 - 1/10, which equals 1/30 cm.

wrong.1: This mistake forgets to use the minus sign for the lens formula.
wrong.2: This mistake incorrectly adds the two reciprocal values together.
wrong.3: This mistake treats the formula as simple subtraction instead of reciprocal addition.

quiz.say: A concave mirror forms an image at 60 centimeters. If the object is placed at 30 centimeters, what is the focal length?
quiz.why: For concave mirrors, both v and u are positive distances, but the focal length f must be negative. Using the formula: 1/f = 1/60 + 1/30 = 3/60 = 1/20. Since it is concave, f = -1/20 cm.

wrong.1: This mistake incorrectly assumes the focal length is positive for concave mirrors.
wrong.2: This mistake only uses the object distance and ignores the image distance.
wrong.3: This mistake incorrectly adds the distances instead of using the reciprocal formula.

quiz.say: If the magnification (m) is -2, what does this tell you about the image?

options.show: The image is half the size and inverted.
options.say: The image is half the size and inverted.

options.show: The image is inverted and twice the size.
options.say: The image is inverted and twice the size.

options.show: The image is upright and twice the size.
options.say: The image is upright and twice the size.

options.show: The image is virtual and twice the size.
options.say: The image is virtual and twice the size.

quiz.why: The negative sign means the image is inverted. The absolute value of two means it is twice the size of the object.

wrong.0: This mistake misinterprets the magnitude of the magnification value.
wrong.2: This mistake ignores the negative sign, suggesting the image is upright.
wrong.3: This mistake confuses the sign of magnification with the image type.
